source_location: Fig. 8b (p. 23898), adsorption branch (filled red squares), marker 24 of 26 resolved
notes: digitized: 90.411149825784 bar, 37.21865639709031 mg/g, archive: fig8b_adsorption.json. Axis unit mg/g, stored as W1 = 0.1 x mg/g. Basis named but not defined: 'to quantify the Gibbs excess amount of hydrogen adsorbed' (p. 23898). BELSORP-HP model printed, manufacturer not printed. Sample mass printed as 'about 0.2 g' (200 mg). isotherm_point_count = 26 resolved adsorption markers only (lower bound): the lowest-pressure adsorption markers merge into an unresolvable stack and the open desorption markers are partly hidden, see log.md. source_location: main-6 (p. 23898), Fig. 8b, open blue squares (desorption), separated marker 7 of 16 (by decreasing pressure)
notes: archive: fig8b_HPCDCM_77K_highP_desorption.json. Digitized 42.632 mg/g at 54.649 bar (axis in mg/g); uptake_wt_pct = W1 = 0.1 x mg/g. Open marker partly covered by red adsorption markers; centre from occlusion-aware template match, archived through digitize_figure.py (log.md). Isotherm I2 = Fig. 8b, high-pressure volumetric BELSORP-HP run on 'about 0.2 g sample' (stored 200 mg). Paper names 'Gibbs excess' but does not define it, so basis_stated = false, basis_inferred = excess. instrument_identified = false: model 'BELSORP-HP' printed without a manufacturer. isotherm_point_count 51 is a lower bound: 26 + 16 separated markers plus >=2 and >=7 markers in two merged red blobs at low pressure; desorption markers hidden under adsorption markers not counted (log.md).
